chapter: Stuff Smith Trio and New York
title: Stuff Smith trio in New York and playing 52nd Street
summary: The trio lasted two to three years, then Jones and Levy worked as a team on 52nd Street with Hawkins, Webster, Parker and Gillespie sitting in.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Tell me about working with Stuff and John. You worked in Chicago how long before you went to New York?

Just about a year, that's all. We weren't together that long. And then we stayed -- we were in New York -- we stayed together maybe two to three years. And then I started working up and down 52nd Street at that point. We used to play with, Ray Perry, the other violinist that was with Lionel Hampton, very good. And after, then I worked with -- they used to hire John and I as a team, because we were on time. We'd show up to work on time, you know, and we wore our uniforms. We kept our home style together. And so we worked with, oh, Don Byas (PHONETIC), Ben Webster, Coleman Hawkins used to sit in with us. Charlie Parker used to sit in with us all the time. Dizzy Gillespie. At that time 52nd Street was -- what do you want to call it -- it was really on then.
That was what year? Or what years?
Well, let's see. I joined Sarah in '47. About '46, you know. And Erroll Garner was there. Oh, there was a whole lot of pleasure there, you know?
